affected_system: land-use planning, public investment, regeneration, and community-benefit system
alternatives: compare eligible treated and credible untreated units for phased regeneration and community-benefit intervention
estimate pre-specified overall and distributional effects of phased regeneration and community-benefit intervention
pair matched neighborhood event-study with resident and business panels with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Parcels, zoning, ownership, development, business, housing, public assets, and population use dated versions.
Scenario capacity and market response are not treated as approved projects or inevitable change.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain pre-intervention conditions for phased regeneration and community-benefit intervention.

constraints.description: The land use, regeneration, and neighborhood change evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: planning director and neighborhood regeneration commissioner
decision_question: Did phased regeneration improve verified access and opportunity without displacement or benefit leakage?
family_title: Land use, regeneration, and neighborhood change

independence_key.binding_constraint: The land use, regeneration, and neighborhood change evaluate must respect declared pre-specified assignment, comparison, outcome, spillover, and subgroup rules.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for phased regeneration and community-benefit intervention passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: matched neighborhood event-study with resident and business panels
independence_key.primary_outcome: change in verified access, stability, and secured community benefits

intended_claim: A versioned evaluate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting phased regeneration and community-benefit intervention, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: change in verified access, stability, and secured community benefits
distributional gap in change in verified access, stability, and secured community benefits
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not infer inclusive growth, well-being, or anti-displacement effects from investment totals alone.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for phased regeneration and community-benefit intervention passes documented checks for dated assignment, comparison validity, pre-trends, outcome panels, attrition, spillovers, and falsification tests.

title: Evaluate regeneration and community-benefit effects
transportability_risks: Planning law, property rights, finance, markets, institutions, and community priorities differ.
Parcel and transaction data may miss informal tenure, businesses, and cultural assets.
